messages:
From: Emma Hart <emma.hart@mercatolabs.com>

Date: Sun, 10 Jan 2027 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Renewal planning — model mix change + capacity ask

Hi Tessa,

Hope you had a good week. We're nearing our renewal and the product team confirmed they're moving one of our high-throughput recommendation paths to a larger long-context model (32k) plus a reranker for top-K reordering. The main asks:

- Reserved capacity to guarantee throughput during peak sales hours (we need consistent p99 latency for <120ms on 1k QPS bursts)
- Add-on for the reranker (we expect ~30% increase in token compute and higher KV cache requirements)
- Term refresh to lock in pricing if we commit to a 12–18 month capacity increase

Can your team share a rough GPU/throughput mapping and any suggested changes to the reserved pool sizes? Procurement will want a draft SOW to start internal approvals.

Thanks — Emma
Emma Hart

emma.hart@mercatolabs.com

From: Tessa Morgan <tessa@redwood.com>

Cc: Diego Fernandez <diego@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 11 Jan 2027 11:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Renewal planning — model mix change + capacity ask

Emma — thanks for the clarity. High level response below; detailed projections attached as a starting point (throughput-projection.xlsx and SOW draft).

Short answer: moving to a 32k-context generator + a reranker will increase reserved GPU needs materially, but we can keep monthly cost growth linear by combining model mix routing, a small burst pool, and a quantized reranker profile. Proposed starting point:

- Reserved pool: 10 H100 equivalent GPUs -> increase to 18 H100 equiv (mix of H100/Hopper+ and an option for A100s for lower-cost runs).
- Burst buffer: +4 GPUs for autoscaling bursts (sits outside the committed pool).
- Throughput target: baseline steady-state for 1k QPS of short-gen requests + scheduled 1k QPS 10-minute bursts for sales windows (we guarantee 95% of tokens under configured p99 latency).
- Reranker: deploy as a separate service tier (dedicated quantized 8-bit profile). Anticipate +25–35% additional token compute; KV cache increase accounted for in memory footprint.

I've attached a preliminary SOW and a spreadsheet that maps request mix -> GPU-hours and estimated monthly commitment. If you want, we can propose an 18-month term that phases the extra reserved GPUs over the first 3 months (50% commit month 1, 100% month 3) to flatten spend and reduce procurement friction.

Next steps:
1) I can loop in our pricing lead for an updated quote (Monica).
2) Diego — can you validate the H100-equivalent mapping for the 32k context path and confirm KV caching assumptions?
3) Emma — if procurement has target dates, share them and we'll prioritize the SOW.

Best,
Tessa Morgan
Account Executive — Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference

From: Diego Fernandez <diego@redwood.com>

Date: Tue, 12 Jan 2027 14:22:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Renewal planning — capacity mapping (technical)

Quick technical note / internal:

- 32k generator: roughly 2.6x memory and 3x token compute vs our current 16k generator baseline for the same batch size (numbers in the spreadsheet).
- Reranker: highly parallelizable but KV-cache heavy during rerank loops; we should reserve an additional 0.8–1.0 GPU equivalence per 5 reranking nodes to keep latency headroom.
- Recommendation: use a mixed-instance pool: 12 H100-equiv dedicated for generator-heavy routes; 6 A100-equiv for reranker/cheap-quantized inference; 4 GPU burst (on-demand) for peak window. This gets to the target p99 with ~10–12% overprovision buffer for safety.

I'll mark the specific rows in throughput-projection.xlsx with our assumptions. Also calling out network egress for repeated rerank calls — Monica please add a line item for bandwidth cost in the SOW.

—Diego
Senior Systems Engineer, Redwood Inference
